_meta.purpose: The per-SKU inputs the cost maths depends on, published so they can be checked. Answers 'how many units are in a case' -- and shows that the workbook holds TWO such numbers measuring different things.

two_case_numbers.Units per case (Item Listing col H, 'Cas: INDIVIDUAL retail units in a shipping case. Cost per CASE multiplies by this. Authoritative for that, confirmed by Justin 2026-07-08.
two_case_numbers.Case size (Item Listing col D, 'Case Siz: Packs per case in the SKU's OWN recorded unit (six-pack = 1, loose bag = 24). Cases made = recorded quantity / this. XLOOKUP'd onto every run sheet, so it is the number on the Source data tab.
two_case_numbers.why they differ: For a multipack, one recorded unit is a 6-pack while a case holds 6 individual boxes. Both numbers are right about different things; applying one where the other belongs moves an answer by the pack count. That is a real defect we have hit (item 47010).

_meta.allergen_column_deliberately_omitted: Item Listing has an 'Allergen' column and it reads 'None' for all 845 rows -- it carries no information. Publishing it would invite reading 'None' as 'this product contains no allergens', which is false for a range where some items contain tree nuts and some contain barley. Allergen facts must come from packaging and CatalogSmith, never from this sheet.
_meta.labor_scope: Pack labor from ACTUAL production runs at the confirmed $26.06/hr production wage. NO ingredients, NO packaging, NO machine overhead -- this is not a landed COGS. Blend lbs/unit is published beside it so the blending side can be checked, but the blend DOLLARS are not in these columns.
_meta.labor_per_case_basis: For a multipack the recorded unit IS the case, so labor per case EQUALS labor per unit -- multiplying by the pack count again would double-count (the item 47010 defect). For a single-unit SKU it is labor per unit x case size. 'Labor $ / item' divides back to one retail item, which is the only basis that compares a multipack against a single fairly.
_meta.channel_pricing_withheld: channel_skus also carries wholesale, distributor and international price-list pricing. This feed publishes to a repository readable by anyone with the link, so only the SKU identifiers are read.

columns.label: Name
columns.basis: The item's name as the Item Listing tab records it.

columns.label: Catalog name
columns.basis: The canonical product name from CatalogSmith's product master, reproduced verbatim. Blank means the Item # does not resolve there, or the master holds a build-default placeholder that is not a real name.

columns.label: Units per case
columns.basis: Item Listing col H 'Case Pack Units' -- INDIVIDUAL retail units in a shipping case. This is what cost per case is multiplied by. Authoritative for that, confirmed 2026-07-08.

columns.label: Case size
columns.basis: Item Listing col D 'Case Size' -- packs per case in THIS SKU's own recorded unit (a six-pack counts as 1, a loose bag as 24). Cases made = recorded quantity / this. It is the value XLOOKUP'd onto the run sheets, so it is the number you see on the Source data tab.

columns.label: Same?
columns.basis: WORKED OUT: whether the two case numbers agree. 'multipack' means they differ because one recorded unit is a pack of several -- expected, not an error, but the place where using the wrong one changes an answer several-fold.

columns.label: Recorded unit
columns.basis: WORKED OUT from the two case numbers and the name: what ONE unit in the quantity columns actually counts.

columns.label: Stocking unit
columns.basis: CatalogSmith: the unit Acctivate stocks this item in (ea / cs / lb). A 'cs' item is counted in CASES in the ERP, so an ERP cost against it is per case, not per unit.

columns.label: Runs
columns.basis: WORKED OUT: production runs recorded for this Item # across both workbooks (task rows excluded).

columns.label: Units recorded
columns.basis: WORKED OUT: sum of Actual Production Quantity over those runs, in the recorded unit above.

columns.label: First run
columns.basis: WORKED OUT from the run rows.

columns.label: Last run
columns.basis: WORKED OUT from the run rows.

columns.label: Stations
columns.basis: WORKED OUT: which stations have run this item.

columns.label: Fill weight (g)
columns.basis: CatalogSmith: the declared net weight of ONE unit, in grams. CatalogSmith owns this -- it is derived from the Acctivate BOM or read off the size in the item name. Use it to sanity-check that a '300g bag' really holds 300g.

columns.label: Blend lbs / unit
columns.basis: POUNDS of blended bulk product in one unit, from the Acctivate BOM. This is the number blending cost is multiplied by, so a wrong one moves the blend side of the cost directly.

columns.label: Blend
columns.basis: The blended bulk product (BBP) this item is made from, per the Acctivate BOM.

columns.label: Labor $ / unit
columns.basis: WORKED OUT from ACTUAL production runs: run hours x operators / units x $26.06. Per ONE RECORDED UNIT -- so for a multipack this is the cost of a whole pack. Pack labor only: no ingredients, no packaging, no overhead.

columns.label: Labor $ / case
columns.basis: WORKED OUT. For a multipack the recorded unit IS the case, so this EQUALS labor per unit -- multiplying again would double-count, which is the mistake item 47010 taught us. For a single-unit SKU it is labor per unit x units per case.

columns.label: Labor $ / item
columns.basis: WORKED OUT: labor for ONE individual retail item -- labor per case divided by units per case. The figure to compare across SKUs, because it is the same basis for a multipack and a single.

columns.label: Case pack (price lists)
columns.basis: CatalogSmith, from the wholesale/distributor price lists: units per case as the PRICE LISTS state it. An INDEPENDENT third opinion -- if it matches 'Units per case', that number is corroborated.

columns.label: Channel SKUs
columns.basis: CatalogSmith: what this Item # is called on each sales channel, for cross-checking against Amazon or Shopify reporting. IDENTIFIERS ONLY -- the price-list pricing on these records is confidential and is not published here.

columns.label: Notes
columns.basis: WORKED OUT: what to be careful about on this row.
